strategyDescription: Primary clustering via GitHub labels (dependencies, workflows, runtime, docs) with semantic grouping for shared label resolution
noveltyRationale: Diverges from first experiment by using concrete GitHub labels as primary clustering signal instead of inferring semantic themes from PR title/body analysis. Groups PRs by tangible delivery area (dependencies, workflow infrastructure, core runtime, docs) for more stable, audit-friendly clusters with 4 major categories.
historicalContext: Previous experiment (runId 37680026048) used semantic-theme-clustering and achieved 85% classification with 3 themes. This experiment reduces to 4 explicit label-based categories to improve cluster stability.

sourceAttempts.notes: Complete Rig workflow with TypeScript-native clustering logic, no agent calls required. Clusters defined explicitly based on GitHub labels and PR content analysis.

clusters.label: Documentation & Sample Programs
clusters.theme: Sample programs, API docs, landing page, README, header updates

clusters.label: Core Runtime & Provider Engines
clusters.theme: Copilot SDK integration, Rig launcher, provider adapters (Pi, Gemini, DeepSeek)

allClusters.theme: Copilot SDK integration, Rig launcher, provider adapters (Pi, Gemini, DeepSeek)

unclassifiedReasons.581: Benchmark decomposition fix - specialized infrastructure work not cleanly mappable to primary categories
unclassifiedReasons.563: Landing diagram layout fix - minor UI/docs improvement without explicit labels

lessonsForNextRun: Label-based clustering provides stable, audit-friendly groups with clear semantics
Some PRs (benchmarking, minor UI fixes) naturally fall outside primary categories despite quality work
Workflow infrastructure and core runtime have significant overlap (8-9 PRs shared) - consider merging in future
Documentation cluster dominates at 40.7% - reflects heavy investment in samples and API clarity this month
Four explicit categories (docs, workflows, runtime, deps) better match human understanding than semantic themes
Next attempt: try time-series clustering (delivery timeline) or ownership-based grouping (team/responsibility areas)
